Third alpha of the `1.4.0` line. This release focuses on the new `langchain.mcp` namespace for adapting MCP servers into LangChain tools.

`MCPAdapter` adapts any target `fastmcp.Client` accepts — a URL, a local script, an in-process server, an `MCPConfig` naming several servers, or a pre-built client — as well as a FastMCP `ClientGroup` for a fleet of servers behind one client.

**`MCPAdapter.list_tools(*, cache_mode="use")`** discovers and adapts tools, with optional client-side response caching (SEP-2549): `use` serves a cached list within the server's TTL hint, `refresh` repopulates it, `bypass` skips it.
**`as_langchain_tool(tool, client, *, elicitation=None)`** converts a single MCP tool for callers managing their own client.

Tool metadata is grouped under an `mcp` namespace on each tool: the tool's `annotations` (snake_case) and `_meta` under `metadata["mcp"]["tool"]`, and the serving server's identity under `metadata["mcp"]["server"]`.
`elicitation="interrupt"` surfaces a server's mid-call questions as LangGraph interrupts, so a human answers and the run resumes.
This is a pre-release; install with `--pre`.
*Release notes curated with the assistance of an AI agent.*
This release adds support for `version="v3"` in `stream_events` / `astream_events` for `langchain` agents. Refer to the event streaming guide for details.

<Prompt description="Migrate a codebase to LangChain v1." icon="arrow-right" actions={["copy"]} Migrate this codebase to LangChain v1 (requires `langchain>=1.0.0`, `langchain-core>=1.0.0`, and Python 3.10+). Key changes: Search the codebase for `create_react_agent`, `pre_model_hook`, `post_model_hook`, `state_modifier`, imports from `langgraph.prebuilt`, and legacy `langchain` modules such as `langchain.chains`, `langchain.retrievers`, `langchain.indexes`, and `langchain.hub`, and apply the necessary changes. Flag anything that cannot be migrated automatically. This guide outlines the major changes between LangChain v1 and previous versions.

Package namespace reduction: the `langchain` package focuses on agents, messages, tools, chat models, and embeddings. Legacy chains, retrievers, indexes, hub, embedding helpers such as `CacheBackedEmbeddings`, and community re-exports moved to `langchain-classic`. Install `langchain-classic` and update those imports to `langchain_classic.*`. Install provider packages directly (for example `langchain-openai`) instead of relying on `langchain` re-exports of community integrations.

`create_react_agent` → `create_agent`: replace `from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent` with `from langchain.agents import create_agent`. Rename `prompt=` to `system_prompt=`. Invoke with `agent.invoke({"messages": [...]})` / `agent.stream(...)`. Prefer `langchain.agents.AgentState` over the deprecated `langgraph.prebuilt` agent state helpers.

Hooks become middleware: replace `pre_model_hook=`, `post_model_hook=`, and `state_modifier=` customization with `create_agent` middleware (`before_model`, `after_model`, `@wrap_model_call`, `@wrap_tool_call`). For human-in-the-loop tool approval, use `HumanInTheLoopMiddleware(interrupt_on={...})` from `langchain.agents.middleware`.

Structured output: keep `response_format=`, but use `ToolStrategy` / `ProviderStrategy` from `langchain.agents.structured_output`. Prompted output forms such as `response_format=("please generate ...", Schema)` are removed.
Streaming node name: when filtering or matching streamed events by node name, rename `"agent"` to `"model"`.
Runtime context: pass static context via the `context=` argument to `invoke` / `stream` (and `context_schema=` on `create_agent`) instead of only `config["configurable"]`.
Standard content blocks: prefer `message.content_blocks` for provider-agnostic content. Existing `message.content` remains valid.

The `langchain` package namespace has been significantly reduced in v1 to focus on essential building blocks for agents. The streamlined package makes it easier to discover and use the core functionality.
If you were using any of the following from the `langchain` package, you'll need to install `langchain-classic` and update your imports: Install with: ---
Retrievers (e.g. `MultiQueryRetriever` or anything from the previous `langchain.retrievers` module)
The hub module (for managing prompts programmatically)

Prior to v1.0, we recommended using @[`langgraph.prebuilt.create_react_agent`][create_react_agent] to build agents. Now, we recommend you use @[`langchain.agents.create_agent`][create_agent] to build agents. The table below outlines what functionality has changed from @[`create_react_agent`] to @[`create_agent`]:

The import path for the agent prebuilt has changed from `langgraph.prebuilt` to `langchain.agents`. The name of the function has changed from @[`create_react_agent`] to @[`create_agent`]: For more information, see Agents.
The `prompt` parameter has been renamed to @[`system_prompt`]:
If using @[`SystemMessage`] objects in the system prompt, extract the string content:

Pre-model hooks are now implemented as middleware with the `before_model` method. This new pattern is more extensible--you can define multiple middlewares to run before the model is called, reusing common patterns across different agents. Post-model hooks are now implemented as middleware with the `after_model` method. This new pattern is more extensible--you can define multiple middlewares to run after the model is called, reusing common patterns across different agents. Common use cases include: v1 has a built in middleware for human in the loop approval for tool calls:

Custom state extends the default agent state with additional fields. You can define custom state in two ways: Defining custom state via middleware is preferred over defining it via @[`state_schema`] on @[`create_agent`] because it allows you to keep state extensions conceptually scoped to the relevant middleware and tools. `state_schema` is still supported for backwards compatibility on `create_agent`.
Via @[`state_schema`] on @[`create_agent`] - Best for state used in tools
Via middleware - Best for state managed by specific middleware hooks and tools attached to said middleware
Use the @[`state_schema`] parameter when your custom state needs to be accessed by tools:

Middleware can also define custom state by setting the @[`state_schema`] attribute. This helps to keep state extensions conceptually scoped to the relevant middleware and tools. See the middleware documentation for more details on defining custom state via middleware.

@[`create_agent`] only supports `TypedDict` for state schemas. Pydantic models and dataclasses are no longer supported. Simply inherit from `langchain.agents.AgentState` instead of `BaseModel` or decorating with `dataclass`. If you need to perform validation, handle it in middleware hooks instead.

Dynamic model selection allows you to choose different models based on runtime context (e.g., task complexity, cost constraints, or user preferences). @[`create_react_agent`] released in v0.6 of `langgraph-prebuilt` supported dynamic model and tool selection via a callable passed to the `model` parameter. This functionality has been ported to the middleware interface in v1.

To better support structured output, @[`create_agent`] no longer accepts pre-bound models with tools or configuration: Dynamic model functions can return pre-bound models if structured output is *not* used.
The @[`tools`][create_agent(tools)] argument to @[`create_agent`] accepts a list of: The argument will no longer accept @[`ToolNode`] instances.
Callable objects (functions) with proper type hints and a docstring
`dict` that represents a built-in provider tools
You can now configure the handling of tool errors with middleware implementing the `wrap_tool_call` method.
Structured output used to be generated in a separate node from the main agent. This is no longer the case. We generate structured output in the main loop, reducing cost and latency.
In v1, there are two new structured output strategies:
`ToolStrategy` uses artificial tool calling to generate structured output

Prompted output is no longer supported via the `response_format` argument. Compared to strategies like artificial tool calling and provider native structured output, prompted output has not proven to be particularly reliable.
When streaming events from agents, the node name has changed from `"agent"` to `"model"` to better reflect the node's purpose.

When you invoke an agent, it's often the case that you want to pass two types of data: In v1, static context is supported by setting the `context` parameter to `invoke` and `stream`. The old `config["configurable"]` pattern still works for backward compatibility, but using the new `context` parameter is recommended for new applications or applications migrating to v1. ---
Dynamic state that changes throughout the conversation (e.g., message history)
Static context that doesn't change during the conversation (e.g., user metadata)

In v1, messages gain provider-agnostic standard content blocks. Access them via @[`message.content_blocks`][content_blocks] for a consistent, typed view across providers. The existing @[`message.content`][BaseMessage(content_blocks)] field remains unchanged for strings or provider-native structures.
New @[`content_blocks`][BaseMessage(content_blocks)] property on messages for normalized content
Standardized block shapes, documented in Messages
Optional serialization of standard blocks into `content` via `LC_OUTPUT_VERSION=v1` or `output_version="v1"`
See the content blocks reference for more details.

Standard content blocks are not serialized into the `content` attribute by default. If you need to access standard content blocks in the `content` attribute (e.g., when sending messages to a client), you can opt-in to serializing them into `content`. Learn more: Messages, Standard content blocks, and Multimodal. ---
All LangChain packages now require Python 3.10 or higher. Python 3.9 reaches end of life in October 2025.

entries.section: Updated return type for chat models
entries.text: The return type signature for chat model invocation has been fixed from @[`BaseMessage`] to @[`AIMessage`]. Custom chat models implementing @[`bind_tools`][BaseChatModel.bind_tools] should update their return signature:

entries.section: Default message format for OpenAI responses API
entries.text: When interacting with the Responses API, `langchain-openai` now defaults to storing response items in message `content`. To restore previous behavior, set the `LC_OUTPUT_VERSION` environment variable to `v0`, or specify `output_version="v0"` when instantiating @[`ChatOpenAI`].

The `max_tokens` parameter in `langchain-anthropic` now defaults to higher values based on the model chosen, rather than the previous default of `1024`. If you relied on the old default, explicitly set `max_tokens=1024`.

Existing functionality outside the focus of standard interfaces and agents has been moved to the `langchain-classic` package. See the Simplified namespace section for details on what's available in the core `langchain` package and what moved to `langchain-classic`.
Methods, functions, and other objects that were already deprecated and slated for removal in 1.0 have been deleted.

Use of the `.text()` method on message objects should drop the parentheses, as it is now a property: Existing usage patterns (i.e., `.text()`) will continue to function but now emit a warning. The method form will be removed in v2.
The `example` parameter has been removed from @[`AIMessage`] objects. We recommend migrating to use `additional_kwargs` for passing extra metadata as needed.

`AIMessageChunk` objects now include a `chunk_position` attribute with position `'last'` to indicate the final chunk in a stream. This allows for clearer handling of streamed messages. If the chunk is not the final one, `chunk_position` will be `None`.
`LanguageModelOutputVar` is now typed to @[`AIMessage`] instead of @[`BaseMessage`].

The logic for merging message chunks (`AIMessageChunk.add`) has been updated with more sophisticated selection handling for the final id for the merged chunk. It prioritizes provider-assigned IDs over LangChain-generated IDs.
We now open files with `utf-8` encoding by default.
Standard tests now use multimodal content blocks.
